
Naming scheme explanation:
    `External` folders in MMF project contain copy pasted files that I didn't write myself.
    Now learned that this is usually called 'Vendor'/'Vendoring'
    (TODO: Maybe centralize explanation or rename to 'Vendor' and delete this explanation. [10 Sep 2026])

[10 Sep 2026]
About ReactiveCocoa and ReactiveSwift (Vendored projects in this folder)
    Background:
        macOS 27 forced raising deployment target from 10.15 -> 12.0
        To avoid this, you have to use build setting `__DIAGNOSE_INVALID_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET_AS_ERROR`, 
        which I don't know how to apply to SPM packages -> Therefore I remove all SPM packages. (And replaced with vendored projects in some cases)
        Also see:
            Commit message of first git commit dealing with this:
                f92d2d53a055bfef747ca939ef8eb453f70168b5
    Version choice:
        ReactiveCocoa 12.0.0 and ReactiveSwift 7.1.1 were what SPM pulled in with dependency 
        rules "Up to next major version" 12.0.0 and 7.0.0 respectively on [10 Sep 2026]|
        (Not quite sure I understand why because ReactiveSwift is on 7.2.1, currently – whatever)
    Vendoring steps:
        1. Copy ReactiveCocoa 12.0.0 and ReactiveSwift 7.1.1 from GitHub and add them to the project
            (Have to copy them via Finder first, not directly via Xcode otherwise it does weird stuff and activates SPM or something.)
        2. Download the Carthage/Checkout/xcconfigs submodule and copy into ReactiveCocoa and ReactiveSwift folders
        3. Go to their .xcodeproj's and ...
            3.1 Add __DIAGNOSE_INVALID_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET_AS_ERROR=NO build setting
            3.2 Increase ReactiveCocoa minimum deployment target from 10.9 -> 10.12 to match ReactiveSwift (otherwise I can't get Xcode to build)
            3.3 Change MACH_O_TYPE to 'Static Library' (size optimization)
                Alternative tested: Add ReactiveSwift and ReactiveCocoa as Dynamic Framework and share between main app and helper -> 16MB (0.2MB larger)
                    I guess the stripping Xcode does for static linking outweighs the duplication
        4. Add the two frameworks as dependencies to Mac Mouse Fix and Mac Mouse Fix Helper targets.
            Choose 'Do not embed' (Embedding unnecessary since it's a 'Static Library')

    Other notes:
        Maybe ReactiveSwift and ReactiveCocoa projects should be in ./Frameworks with Sparkle?
            The 'External' folders are more for files we're using directly in our code but haven't written ourselves.

    On general size optimization:
        (Discovered this after noticing size increase after vendoring ReactiveCocoa and ReactiveSwift, but not inherently related)
            (TODO: Move to different doc)

        - ENABLE_TESTABILITY=YES prevented symbol stripping and caused size bloat, I think especially after vendoring ReactiveSwift and ReactiveCocoa (Or maybe I just noticed it then)
            - Had enabled this in `9e6af66bb5cf9fcc45bc18e6d6a48b1ce68b746d`. I don't remember why.
        - Setting DEPLOYMENT_POSTPROCESSING=YES for Release makes executables even smaller (strips symbols, even better than -Wl,-s)
        - Also set COPY_PHASE_STRIP=YES for Release in hopes of shrinking Sparkle.framework, but didn't make a difference.
        - Also see:
            SO question about static frameworks not being stripped which I though I was encountering: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/75917818/xcode-doesnt-strip-unused-symbol-for-static-framework
